title: VTree: Question-Driven Growth of Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Long-Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2611.28093v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long videos spanning tens of minutes to hours far exceed the context window of today's vision-language models, and the standard remedy of sparse uniform frame sampling discards exactly the fine-grained evidence that specific questions depend on. Existing video agents explore on demand but re-explore from scratch for every question and discard their exploration state once an answer is produced, so per-question cost scales with video length. Hierarchical-memory methods instead fix the scope of each depth in advance and deepen along a pre-committed pyramid rather than toward the question. We observe that a video's coarse structure (where its scenes and topics begin and end) is question-independent, whereas which part a question must zoom into, and how deep, is question-dependent. translated_title: VTree：面向智能体长视频理解的问题驱动式层次记忆增长
translated_abstract: 跨越数十分钟到数小时的长视频远远超出了当今视觉语言模型的上下文窗口，而标准的稀疏均匀帧采样方法恰恰丢弃了特定问题所依赖的细粒度证据。现有的视频智能体虽然按需探索，但每个问题都要从头重新探索，并在生成答案后丢弃探索状态，因此单个问题的成本随视频长度而增加。层次记忆方法则事先固定每个深度的范围，沿预先确定的金字塔向下加深，而不是朝向问题本身加深。我们观察到，视频的粗粒度结构（其场景和主题的起止位置）与问题无关，而问题需要放大到哪一部分、深入到什么程度则与问题相关。我们提出VTree，它在视频上一次性构建粗粒度的层次记忆树，然后针对每个问题，只在该问题需要更深入理解的分支处进行增长。
tldr: VTree先一次性构建与问题无关的粗粒度层次记忆树，再针对每个问题只在需要之处动态增长分支，从而以远低于现有方法的成本实现对长视频的高精度问答理解。
en_tdlr: VTree builds a question-independent coarse hierarchical memory tree once, then dynamically grows branches only where each question needs deeper evidence, enabling efficient and accurate agentic long-video understanding at far lower per-question cost.
